A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same robotics foundation-model survey. Their text, tables, figures, and references support comparison, including v2's Appendices A–I, which retain substantial material previously in the main text.

before.justification: Section 2 and Figure 1 report the authors' bibliometric analysis of their selected literature, including article-type percentages and publication-venue counts. These are original descriptive data-analysis results, although no robot benchmarking is performed.

after.justification: Appendix B and Figure 7 retain the survey's original bibliometric analysis. The stated absence of empirical benchmarking concerns comparisons of robotic methods and does not negate these descriptive results.

M1.justification: Neither version introduces a proposed robotic algorithm or model. Revised classifications, including replacing pre-training with supervised learning in the learning-paradigm taxonomy, change the survey's organization and interpretation of existing methods.

E1.justification: No training or evaluation coverage changes. Newly discussed resources such as EPIC-KITCHENS and Ego-Exo4D are literature examples, not datasets used in new experiments. The five detailed task-specific dataset catalogs are retained in Appendix I.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a proposed method. The model catalogs and comparisons with other surveys are qualitative literature comparisons, not experimentally evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: The reported literature sample changes from 435 articles in v1 Section 2.3 to 438 in v2 Section 2 and Appendix B.3. The illustrative Scopus query also changes 'visual foundation model' to 'vision foundation model'; this documents a revised query without establishing that the search was rerun.

E4.justification: Neither version supplies original ablations, robustness experiments, or experimental case studies. The added dataset-gap and open-problem discussions are interpretive synthesis; relocating detailed literature reviews does not introduce supplementary experiments.

E5.justification: The bibliometric charts retain the same descriptive reporting. No repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or removed.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes reported CLIP parameters from 175M to 428M and SAM parameters from 1.2B to 636M, and revises model-type and embodiment classifications. The selected-literature total changes from 435 to 438, while the bibliometric charts remain unchanged. These are descriptive catalog changes, not performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version presents new mathematical results, derivations, or proofs. The revised descriptions of embodiment, research phases, and supervised learning are conceptual classifications rather than formal mathematical definitions.

C1.justification: The central five-phase, six-criterion survey contribution remains. The abstract and introduction recast the dataset contribution as a synthesis of dataset families, uses, and gaps, and explicitly clarify that quantitative benchmarking falls outside the survey's scope.

C2.justification: Section 11 adds dataset-family-specific limitations, while Sections 13–14 connect challenges to remedies, distinguish partial progress from unresolved problems, and prioritize nearer- and longer-term goals. v2 also explicitly discusses the survey's coverage limitations, distinguishes standalone models from FM-based systems, and revises the learning-paradigm taxonomy.

D1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix B newly disclose LLM-assisted literature-gap checking and manual inclusion and reference verification, and clarify the search strategy. Table 2 changes Gemini Robotics' reported public-availability flag from Y to N; the PDFs do not establish an actual resource withdrawal.

R1.justification: v2 adds Caron et al. (2021) for DINO and references for EPIC-KITCHENS, Ego-Exo4D, and COM Kitchens. Sections 1 and 3.1 refine comparisons with earlier surveys, particularly their benchmarking coverage and relationship to the proposed five-phase chronology.

P1.justification: Sections 5–10 are extensively condensed and rewritten, with detailed reviews retained in Appendices C–H. Methodology and dataset documentation move to Appendices B and I. Expanded concluding synthesis and systematic appendix cross-references substantially restructure the narrative.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a compact summary, with the detailed comparison retained as Table 8. Table 2 gains a category column, comparative tables are compressed, and timeline and taxonomy graphics are revised. Dataset tables and bibliometric plots move to appendices; representative-method images are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the survey easier to navigate and better qualified through clearer model/system and learning-paradigm distinctions, dataset-family synthesis, and explicit coverage limitations. Detailed reviews remain available in the appendices. These changes improve clarity and interpretability, although much of the supporting analysis and the central conclusions were already present in v1.
